Related Ross Names Bank of America Official Bank of CityPlace
summary:
Related Ross has named Bank of America the Official Bank of CityPlace through a multiyear partnership that includes a future on site retail presence in the district, community events, and financial wellness programming.
The partnership brings together two organizations with longstanding ties to Palm Beach County. Bank of America and Merrill have served the county for more than 100 years, working with individuals, businesses, and nonprofit organizations across the region. Related Ross has invested in West Palm Beach for nearly three decades, including the development of CityPlace and its ongoing work across downtown.
The partnership comes as West Palm Beach continues to grow as a center for business, residential life, hospitality, and culture, with CityPlace at the heart of that evolution. It builds on both companies’ longstanding presence in the region, bringing Bank of America into CityPlace’s year roundyear-round community programming while creating new opportunities for the organizations to collaborate across West Palm Beach.
“There is a natural alignment in how our two organizations think about West Palm Beach and its innovative future,” said Webber Hudson, Executive Vice President, Related Ross. “As the city continues to evolve, we want CityPlace to remain a place that brings people together. We’re excited to launch this first phase with Bank of America and look forward to sharing more as our partnership grows.”
West Palm Beach has transformed into one of the country’s most dynamic growth markets, attracting companies and talent from industries ranging from technology and financial services to defense tech and advanced manufacturing. In the second quarter of 2026, Bank of America provided nearly two billion dollars$2 billion in loans to small and commercial businesses in Palm Beach County to support local employers and economic growth.
“As Palm Beach County continues to grow, Bank of America is investing in the people, organizations and businesses that help power its future,” said Fabiola Brumley, president, Bank of America Palm Beach County. “With nearly 1,000 teammates across the market, including Merrill, we’re here to support our customers and clients, help businesses start, grow and succeed, and contribute to job creation and long termlong-term economic growth. We work closely with entrepreneurs and business leaders to provide the capital, expertise and connections they need to expand and open new doors throughout the region. Partnerships like this build on that work by strengthening our communities and expanding opportunity.”
Bringing the partnership to life at CityPlace
The partnership will include several integrations across CityPlace’s year roundyear-round programming and public spaces, including:
CityPlace Retail Presence: Bank of America and Related Ross plan to roll out Bank of America retail offerings, including A T MsATMs at CityPlace. Locations and timing will be announced.
Holiday programming: Bank of America will be the presenting partner for CityPlace’s 2027 holiday programming, including the Santa Experience and Family Movie Nights on the lawn.
District Fit: Bank of America will support financial wellness programming during CityPlace’s annual spring wellness festival.
Women’s Entrepreneur Market: Bank of America will be the presenting partner for the market during Related Ross’ annual Women’s Leadership event in March, providing a platform for businesses and entrepreneurs, largely led by women.
The partnership builds on CityPlace’s existing calendar of public events and nonprofit collaborations. Related Ross works with local businesses, educational institutions and organizations throughout the year on arts, wellness and family programming, including its recent Community Block Party benefiting Alexander W. Dreyfoos School of the Arts.
A shared commitment to Palm Beach County
Related Ross and Bank of America also have longstanding philanthropic ties to the region. Through the Related Ross Foundation, Related Ross works with local organizations on education, workforce development, neighborhood initiatives and arts and culture, with a particular focus on the Historic Northwest, Coleman Park and Pleasant City. Through 2026, Related Ross pledged more than fifteen million dollars$15 million in charitable contributions to organizations serving West Palm Beach.
Since 2020, Bank of America has provided eight million dollars$8 million in philanthropic support across Palm Beach County, while local employees have contributed 81,400 volunteer hours to help address community needs. The bank recently committed five hundred thousand dollars$500,000 to the planned African American Museum and Research Library in West Palm Beach.
The organizations plan to add programming at CityPlace and other Related Ross properties in West Palm Beach.

Sygnum Launches ETH Alpha Fund as Investors Look to Grow ETH Holdings Beyond Staking
summary:
Sygnum, a global digital asset banking group, today announced the launch of the Sygnum ETH Alpha Fund SP, giving professional investors a regulated way to grow their ETH holdings beyond staking. The market-neutral fund, denominated in ETH, targets annual returns of 8-10% in ETH, net of fees, and opened to investors on 2 November. 
Corporate treasuries and exchange-traded funds are now among the largest stakers of ETH, and staking rewards of around 2-3% a yearⁱⁱ have become the standard return on institutional ETH holdings. Building on this, long term ETH investors aim to increase ETH holdings without selling it or taking a view on its price. 
The fund keeps its core holdings staked natively with Sygnum, earning protocol rewards, and adds three further return sources, each with a different driver: premium from options, arbitrage between trading venues, and carry as well as funding rates in derivatives markets. These strategies are run by underlying managers who already operate them in other currencies, such as USD. All profit and loss is realized and reported in ETH, so investors grow the amount of ETH they hold rather than converting into dollar yield. As the fund is denominated in ETH, investors remain fully exposed to the ETH price, while the strategies themselves are market-neutral. 
“Institutions that hold ETH for the long term increasingly think in ETH, not dollars, and judge their year by whether they end it holding more. We built the fund around that measure, adding in-kind income strategies to staking within the safeguards of a regulated structure.” said Markus Hämmerli, Head of Asset Management and ETH Alpha Fund lead at Sygnum. 
With attractive subscription and redemption terms, a disciplined risk management framework and off-exchange safekeeping through Sygnum Protect, the fund is designed for professional and institutional investors seeking quality yield opportunities within an institutional-grade structure. The fund is managed by Sygnum Asset Management, a subdivision of Sygnum Bank AGs Investment Solutions department. 
The ETH Alpha Fund is Sygnum’s second alpha fund in just over a year, following the launch of the Starboard Sygnum BTC Alpha Fund in October 2025, and meets growing demand from investors for returns earned and paid in the digital assets they already hold.

content: Digital asset banking group Sygnum has launched the Sygnum ETH Alpha Fund SP to help professional investors grow their ETH holdings beyond traditional staking. The market-neutral fund aims to deliver annualized returns in ETH through a combination of native staking, options premiums, trading arbitrage, and derivatives strategies. Designed for institutional clients, the regulated fund allows investors to increase their ETH volume while maintaining full exposure to the asset's price.
